picks.title: Audible's new features let you explore book worlds — and use AI to talk to characters
picks.excerpt: Audible is rolling out features that track characters, surface places and imagery mentioned in books, and let listeners interact with characters via generative AI.
picks.rationale: A major platform launch: Audible ships character tracking, world exploration and generative-AI character chat for listeners. It changes how audiobooks are consumed and adds a new rights question for authors.

picks.title: Innovation with AI Abounds: The International Digital Publishing Award Announces 12 Finalists
picks.excerpt: The International Digital Publishing Award names 12 finalists dominated by AI projects (AI translation, audiobooks, dyslexia tools); winners announced at Frankfurter Buchmesse next week.
picks.rationale: A new official announcement: a shortlist of real AI publishing products (translation, audio, accessibility) ahead of Frankfurt. It works as a map of what is shipping in the industry.

picks.title: Opus 5.5 loves to tell you 'this matters' (and other AI writing tells)
picks.excerpt: An analysis of model-specific prose tells finds Opus 5.5's biggest giveaway is the word 'dependable', used 23x more often than in human writing samples.
picks.rationale: Practical for writers and editors: it quantifies the verbal tics of specific models. That ties into the running debates on AI disclosure and detection, but it is a new data-driven analysis.

picks.title: Korean Manhwa Apocalypse: Hidden Risks Behind Chinese AI Comic Dramas' Global Expansion
picks.excerpt: As Korean manhwa's overseas boom fades, Chinese AI-generated comic dramas are scaling globally, posing hidden risks to the webcomic business.
picks.rationale: A comics/webtoon angle with direct relevance to Korean readers: Chinese AI comic dramas are scaling against manhwa exports. This is a market shift, not a rehash of the Webtoon partnership or Novvel cards.

picks.title: AI narration companies are the audiobook industry's Trojan horse
picks.excerpt: Audio specialist Jessica Barnfield argues AI voice firms like ElevenLabs aren't widening access to audiobooks so much as gathering publishers' data.
picks.rationale: A specific argument from an audio-industry practitioner: AI narration deals such as ElevenLabs' work as data-gathering for the vendors. This is a new angle, not a recap of the Spotify narration or De Marque deal news.
